texts.preamble: Smt.M.Jyothi vs Sri.M.Saravana on 2 February, 2021 Crl. Appeal No.1850/2018 1 In The Court Of Lxvii Addl City Civil And Sessions Judge; Bengaluru City (CCH.No.68) Present Sri.K.Subramanya, B.Com., Ll.M. Lxvii Addl City Civil & Sessions Judge , Bengaluru . Dated this the 2 nd day of February 2021. Appellants : 1. Smt.M.Jyothi, W/o.M.Saravana, 35 years. 2. S.Chaithanya, D/o.M.Saravana, 14 years. 3. S.Subramanya, S/o.M.Saravana, 10 years.
texts.facts: This Memorandum of Appeal is preferred by the appellant under Section 29 of PWDV Act challenging the order passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Traffic Court-V, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.364/2011, dated:18.07.2018 as to dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 12 of PWDV Act. 2. The appellants herein were the petitioners and the respondents herein was the respondents before the trial Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 court. For the sake of convenience, parties would be referred to by the ranks they were assigned before the trial court. 3. Brief facts of the case are as under: The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.1 was solemnized on 4.02.2004 at Sri Vasavi Kannika Parameshwari Prathana Kalyana Mantapa as per Hindu customs and rites. During their marital relationship, they begotten two children. At the time of marriage, the parents of the petitioner No.1 had given jewellary of 180 grams, cash of Rs.1,00,000/- to the respondent No.1 apart from incurring marriage expenses. After the marriage, the petitioner No.1 started to reside with the respondent No.1 in the matrimonial home. During her stay in the matrimonial home, the respondents started mental torture to her and on many occasions, the respondent No.1 has assaulted her brutally and caused bleeding injuries. It is also alleged that the respondent No.1 used to beat her with clubs on her face, leg and on other parts of the body, however she tolerated all this with the fond hope that the respondent No.1 may change his attitude. The respondent No.4 though marriage, used to reside with the respondent Nos.1 to 3 and the respondent Nos.2 to 4 used to instigate the respondent No.1 to assault on the petitioner Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 No.1/appellant No.1. They have abused her in filthy language and demanded more dowry from her parents house. The respondent No.1 took care of the children and their education. He failed to provide day-to-day necessities ad medical expenses of the petitioners. In spite of panchayats is convened, the respondent No.1 used to tender his apology and tae back the petitioners. In spite of it, the torture and inhuman treatment continued. In the month of May 2011, the respondent No.1 has thrown her out from the matrimonial house and hence, she has lodged the complaint before the police, but the police have not taken any action. The matrimonial relationship between herself and respondent No.1 was completely broken. There is no safety to the life of petitioners in th hands of the respondent No.1. Hence, from May 2011, she is residing at her parents house along with her children. She has no source of income. Hence, she is under difficulties to manage the day-to-day necessities of herself and her children. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 is working as Fitter in Sogeshi MNR Filteration Indian Pvt. Ltd., and getting the monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-. Apart from that, the respondent No.1 has let out the premises on rent Smt.M.Jyothi vs Sri.M.Saravana on 2 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120447495/ 2 and getting Rs.20,000/- per month. He is also owning a Saloon Shop and earning Rs.15,000/- per month. The total income of the respondent No.1 is at Rs.50,000/- per Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 month. In spite of it, he is neglected and refused to give maintenance and expenses to the petitioner No.1 and her children. Hence, the petitioner No.1 has filed the petition under Section 12 of PWDV Act. After due process and procedure, the trial court has dismissed the petition filed by the petitioners. Hence, this appeal. The contention taken before the trial court by the respondents is manifestly erroneous and the trial court ought not to have dismissed the petition. The trial court has grossly erred in law and not appreciated that the respondent No.1 has harassed and tortured the appellant No.1 and failed to pay the maintenance. There is severe threat to the appellant and the said fact has been overlooked by the trial court. The trial court has failed to observe that the appellant No.1 was residing in the portion of the house and the respondents during her stay, used to harass and torture her and thrown her out of the house and when the panchayat was convened, the appellant was been provided Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 with shelter and subsequently continued to harass her. The respondent No.1 has suppressed the material facts before the trial court just to escape from providing shelter and to pay the maintenance and compensation. The appellant has proved prima-facie case against the respondent No.1 and the trial court has not considered the same and dismissed the petition. The respondent No.1 has filed a petition for restitution of conjugal right before the Family Court and the same was allowed. In spite of it, the respondent No.1 did not maintain the appellant and continued to harass and torture her. Hence, the petition is filed and the trial court without considering the reliefs under Section 12 of PWDV Act, has dismissed the petition. There was an interim order of granting maintenance of Rs.3,000/- per month, but while passing the order on merit, the petition itself is dismissed. The appellant/petitioner is facing financial crises and starvation. The appellant is an Unemployee and Uneducated woman and she has to maintain her children i.e., appellant Nos.2 & 3 and has to take care care of the education of the children, who are pursuing studies in Holy Child Convent and Holy Kids School. There are several weaknesses and contradictions in the contention of the respondent, which have been over looked by the trial court. Hence, sought for setting aside the impugned order by Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 allowing this appeal. The respondent No.1 was not invited by the petitioner No.1 for 5th year birthday celebration of their daughter i.e., appellant No.2/petitioner No.2.
texts.arguments: 4. In the grounds, the appellant/petitioner No.1 has contended that the trial court has erred in dismissing the petition and it is illegal, invalid, improper and not in accordance with law and hence, liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The trial court has placed much reliance on the unacceptable contention of the respondents, which are inadmissible. Under such circumstances, Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 the trial court has relied upon the dictum of the Hon'ble High Court of Rajasthan in Crl. Mis. (Pet.) No.1524/2011 (Sudama Dutt Sharma .Vs. State of Rajasthan) , wherein Their Lordships have clearly held that, "in the absence of concrete proof relating to the instance of domestic violence, a casual reference of name of family members without their being any allegation of their active involvement in the matter is sufficient to conclude that the complaint is in-fact designed to harass the respondents" . The natural guardian of a Hindu minor, in respect of the minor's person as well as in respect of the minor's property (excluding his or her undivided interest in joint family property), are-- (a) in the case of a boy or an unmarried Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 girl--the father, and after him, the mother: provided that the custody of a minor who has not completed the age of five years shall ordinarily be with the mother; 17. The concept and proposition of Section 13 in The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 is to be considered, which reads thus : Welfare of minor to be paramount consideration.-- ( 1) In the appointment or declaration of any person as guardian of a Hindu minor by a court, the welfare of the minor shall be the paramount consideration. (c) The loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person ; and (d) the maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(2 of 1974) or any other law for the Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 time being in force. (2) The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed. (3) The Magistrate shall have the power to order an appropriate lump sum payment or monthly payments of maintenance, as the nature and circumstances of the case may require. (4) The Magistrate shall send a copy of the order for monetary relief made under sub-section (1) to the parties to the application and to the in-charge of the Police Station within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the respondent resides. (5) The respondent shall pay the monetary relief granted to the aggrieved person within the period specified in the order under sub-section (1). (6) Upon the failure on the part of the respondent to make payment in terms of the order under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may direct the employer or a debtor of the respondent, to directly pay to the aggrieved person or to deposit with the court a portion of the wages or salaries or debt due to or accrued to the credit of the respondent, which amount may be adjusted towards the monetary relief payable by the Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 respondent. 19. In the decision reported in 1991(2) SCC 375 (K.Vimala .Vs. Veeraswamy ), Their Lordships have clearly observed as under: Section 125 of the code of Criminal Procedure is meant to achieve a social purpose. The object is to prevent vagrancy and destitution. It provides a speedy remedy for the supply of food, clothing and shelter to the deserted wife. The woman not having the legal status of a wife is thus brought within the inclusive definition of the term "Wife" consistent with the objective. Thus, man who lived with woman for a long time made liable to pay maintenance. The man should not be allowed enjoy advantage of a de-facto marriage without undertaking the duties and obligations. Any other interpretation would lead the woman to "vagrancy and destitution" Smt.M.Jyothi vs Sri.M.Saravana on 2 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120447495/ 8 which the provision of maintenance under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., is meant to prevent". 20. In another decision reported in (2014) ACR 436 (Shamim Bano .Vs. Asraf Khan) , Their Lordships have clearly observed as under: "Another aspect which has to be kept uppermost in mind is that when the marriage breaks up, a woman suffers from emotional fractures, fragmentation Crl.Appeal No.1850/2018 of sentiments, loss of economic and social security and in certain cases, inadequate requisites for survival. A marriage is fundamentally a unique bond between two parties. When it perishes like a mushroom, the dignity of the female fame gets corroded. It is the law's duty to recompense and primary obligation is that of a husband. Needless to emphasize the entitlement and necessitous provisions have to be made in accordance with the parameters of law". 21. In another decision reported in 1982 Criminal Law Journal 485 (Basanta Kumari Mohanty .Vs. Sarat Kumar Mohanty) , Their Lordshis have clearly observed as under: "The object of the provisions being to prevent vagrancy and destitution, it has to be found out as to what is required by the wife to maintain a standard of living which is neither luxurious nor penurious; but is modestly consistent with the status of the family. The needs and requirements of the wife, child or parents for a moderate living, the earnings of the husband, son or father or his capacity to earn and his commitments are relevant factors". 22.
